reading.body:
Equinix DC15 is a 115,604-square-foot colocation facility in Ashburn, Virginia, part of the operator's 15-building Washington DC metro campus, the largest single metro region by facility count in the company's portfolio. The facility is positioned within North America's primary peering point and a major gateway to European connectivity, but Equinix publishes no megawatt capacity figure for this building on its specification page. The cooling infrastructure is specified at N+20% redundancy, a standard tier that qualifies the facility for enterprise workloads but does not indicate the IT load density or total power draw.

In Virginia, DC15 ranks 24th among all 23 facilities with published megawatt figures in the state, meaning Equinix has disclosed power capacity for other Virginia sites but not for this one. Virginia contains 326 mapped data center facilities across the state, of which only 23 publish power specifications, totaling 1,375 megawatts. Without a published power capacity, DC15 cannot be sized relative to the state's disclosed infrastructure or against other major AI training campuses.

The Ashburn metro cluster's dominance in regional peering and European connectivity makes it strategically relevant to AI workloads requiring low-latency model serving and real-time inference, but Equinix does not publish the power or rack density figures needed to assess whether DC15 itself is sized for large-scale AI training or serves as a supporting colocation facility in the larger campus ecosystem.
